title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki (with Sharon Lechter)
blurb: Robert Kiyosaki tells the story of growing up in Hawaii with two father figures. His own father was highly educated and held a respected government job, yet he struggled with money all his life. His best friend's father left school early but built real wealth through businesses and property. Through the lessons of this rich dad, Kiyosaki argues that schools teach people to work for money but rarely teach how money actually works. He urges readers to learn the difference between assets, which put money in your pocket, and liabilities, which take money out. He warns that fear and desire keep people trapped in a cycle of earning and spending that he calls the rat race. His answer is financial literacy, steadily building assets, and choosing work for what it teaches rather than just the paycheck.

lessons.t: The Rich Don't Work for Money
lessons.b: Through young Robert's low-paid job at rich dad's store, the book shows how fear and desire keep people chasing paychecks, and why learning to make money work for you is the way out of the rat race.
Wealth comes from building a column of assets that put money in your pocket, like businesses and rental property, rather than buying liabilities, including a home you live in, which take money out.

Your profession is not your business, so keep your day job while steadily building your own column of assets, much as McDonald's grew rich from the land under its restaurants and not only from selling burgers.
issues: scene 6: The 'RUNS WITHOUT YOU' caption under Business and the 'ASSETS' label under the coin bin are very small, about 16px at 1600 width. That is below the 18px minimum, and the 'ASSETS' label is crowded against the bottom of the bin. (fix: Raise both labels to at least 20px. Move the 'ASSETS' label about 10px further below the bin so it has clear spacing.)

lessons.t: Taxes and the Power of Corporations
lessons.b: Understanding tax law and using corporations lets the rich earn, spend, and then pay tax on what remains, while employees are taxed before they ever see their pay.
Financial knowledge lets you see deals others miss and create your own luck, such as buying property cheaply when a market crashes and everyone else is afraid.

lessons.t: Work to Learn, Not to Earn
lessons.b: Choose jobs for the skills they teach, especially selling, communication and managing systems, because many people can cook a better burger than McDonald's but few can build the business behind it.
issues: scene 1: An outlined rectangle sits half-hidden behind the reporter figure's torso. It reads as a stray or broken shape stacked under the body rather than a recognisable notebook or laptop. (fix: Move the notepad fully clear of the figure, e.g. held in front at chest height with a visible hand or placed on the table line beside her, and give it a few ruled lines so it reads as a notebook. Otherwise remove it.)

lessons.b: Cynicism, laziness, bad habits and arrogance hold people back, and simple shifts like paying yourself first and asking how you can afford something help you break through them.
issues: scene 1: The picture contradicts the narration. The four habits are shown as approved items with amber checkmarks, and an arrow runs from them straight to ASSETS. That reads as 'these habits lead to assets', when the narration says they block people from building assets. (fix: Remove the checkmarks, or replace them with indigo X marks. Draw the four habit boxes as a stacked wall placed between the financially literate figure and the ASSETS box. Make the dashed path stop at the wall, so the arrow to ASSETS is visibly blocked.)
